title: Chip stocks bounce back after a hard fall
summary: Shares of chip companies rose on Friday after a sharp drop the day before. AMD gained about 11%. Reports said the bounce won back part of the earlier losses, but analysts warned that prices could keep swinging.
why: When a group of stocks falls fast and then jumps, it is often investors catching their breath, not a sign of what comes next. For a beginner, the lesson is that big one day moves in both directions are normal for chip stocks, so check how far a stock still is from its high before getting excited.

title: US stocks rise on Friday but the week still ends lower
summary: The S&P 500 gained about 0.3% and the Nasdaq about 1.1% on Friday, a partial recovery from the day before. The Dow slipped slightly. Reports said worries about tighter rules for the AI industry had hit stocks earlier in the week.
why: The S&P 500 is a basket of 500 big US companies, so it shows the mood of the whole market. A small gain after a big drop means the market is still nervous. It helps to look at a whole week, not just one day.

title: Strong jobs report pushes Treasury yields higher
summary: Reports said October's job gains were stronger than expected, and that this lifted Treasury yields and the odds that interest rates stay high or rise. Higher yields give investors a safe alternative to stocks.
why: When the government pays more interest on its bonds, stocks have to look better to compete. Fast growing tech companies are hit the most, because their profits are expected far in the future and high rates make future money worth less today.
